run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested custom-CRD runbook does not exist for this target (fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND; the only approved runbook is service-troubleshooting, which does not match this problem), so no runbook steps could be executed. What the evidence does show: the WhaleWatcher CRD (whalewatchers.ocean.io, group ocean.io, namespaced, single served/storage version v1) exists and declares no status subresource, and the operator workload whale-operator in namespace app-96 is up and healthy (1/1 ready, pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-p2vsq Running/Ready since 2026-11-21T07:24:45Z, 0 restarts, no crash or failed-mount events). The strongest supported configuration finding is that the identity the operator runs as holds only read access: ClusterRole whale-operator grants solely apiGroups [ocean.io], resources [whalewatchers], verbs [get,list,watch]; it is the only ClusterRole in the cluster whose rules mention whalewatchers, and the only ClusterRoleBinding whose subjects reference 'app-96' or 'whale' is the one binding it to ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator. A reconciler therefore cannot persist status or any other write through that identity. I could not observe the resulting denied write (the operator container produced 0 log lines in the whole window, the operator source sits in an unreadable Secret, WhaleWatcher objects cannot be listed with the available tools, and both Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable), so that remains a leading hypothesis rather than a confirmed root cause. The whole app-96 stack (namespace 07:24:43Z, CRD/Deployment/ServiceAccount/ClusterRoleBinding 07:24:43-44Z, ReplicaSet and pod 07:24:44-45Z) is only about 40 seconds older than the first observation, so nothing about earlier behavior in the 24h window is knowable.

claims.text: The CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists: group ocean.io, names WhaleWatcher (plural whalewatchers), scope Namespaced, one version v1 that is served and storage, and its spec contains no subresources block, i.e. no status subresource; created 2026-11-21T07:24:44Z.

ClusterRole whale-operator contains exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"]. It contains no update, patch or create verb and no rule for any other resource kind.
Of the 85 ClusterRoles returned, whale-operator is the only one whose rules mention whalewatchers, so no second ClusterRole grants wider access to ocean.io/whalewatchers.

ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ClusterRole whale-operator to the subject ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96, and it is the only ClusterRoleBinding among the 72 examined whose subjects reference 'app-96' or 'whale'.
ServiceAccount whale-operator exists in namespace app-96 (created 2026-11-21T07:24:44Z), and the operator pod runs under serviceAccountName whale-operator with a projected in-cluster token volume.

Deployment app-96/whale-operator has generation 1, 1 requested replica, readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, with container command ["python","/app/operator.py"], image python:3.9-slim, serviceAccountName whale-operator, and the operator code supplied by a Secret-backed volume mounted at /app.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-p2vsq is Phase Running, condition Ready=True since 2026-11-21T07:24:45Z, container operator restartCount 0 with no lastState termination, owned by ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 which is owned by Deployment whale-operator.

The whole whale stack is younger than the incident window's start: namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-21T07:24:43Z, and the CRD, ServiceAccount, ClusterRoleBinding and Deployment were created 2026-11-21T07:24:43-44Z, with the ReplicaSet and pod at 07:24:44-45Z.

The cluster-wide events query returned only 6 events, all Normal and all about the operator pod's creation: Deployment app-96/whale-operator reason ScalingReplicaSet (scaled replica set to 1), ReplicaSet app-96/whale-operator-5f695b7c66 reason SuccessfulCreate, and Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-p2vsq reasons Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started. No event in that returned set involves a WhaleWatcher object, a failed mount, an RBAC denial or a crash.
The cluster-wide NetworkPolicy query returned an empty list (0 items processed), so no NetworkPolicy object was returned that could deny the operator's traffic to the API server.
The ValidatingWebhookConfiguration query returned an empty list (0 items processed), so no validating admission webhook was returned that could be rejecting writes to WhaleWatcher objects.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready (KubeletReady) with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, and the kube-system control plane plus coredns pods (coredns-559f6c778d-bwl2n, coredns-559f6c778d-lfqlc) are Running and Ready, so scheduling pressure and DNS/control-plane unavailability are not supported by these readings.

Leading candidate: reconciliation cannot persist its result because the operator's only granted identity (ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator via ClusterRole whale-operator) holds just get/list/watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers and no update/patch/create anywhere; because the CRD declares no status subresource, writing .status requires update or patch on whalewatchers itself, which the role does not grant, so such a write would be rejected as Forbidden and the CR status would never change. The denial itself was not observed (no operator logs, no apiserver metrics available), so this is unconfirmed.

Second candidate: if the reconciler in the Secret-supplied /app/operator.py patches the whalewatchers/status subresource, that request would fail because the CRD version v1 defines no subresources, independent of RBAC; the operator code and its API version cannot be read (Secret not readable), so this cannot be confirmed or ranked against the RBAC candidate.

Third candidate: the WhaleWatcher objects said to be unreconciled may not exist in app-96 or may predate this snapshot, since the namespace itself was created 2026-11-21T07:24:43Z and the custom resources could not be listed with the available tools; without them neither their spec nor their empty status can be read.

The operator pod itself shows no failure on its own signals: Phase Running, Ready=True, restartCount 0, no lastState termination, no FailedMount/FailedScheduling/CrashLoop events, so 'the operator pod is broken or restarting' is not supported by pod state or events.

Admission webhooks and network-level blocking are not supported as causes here: the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and NetworkPolicy queries both returned empty lists, and the node is Ready with no memory, disk or PID pressure.

Rejected: that the operator deployment was rolled out or restarted over an unchanged pod template during the incident, i.e. that a rollout is the fault. The Deployment is generation 1 with a single ReplicaSet created together with the Deployment at 07:24:44Z, the pod has restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, and the only events are that first creation sequence, so there is no replacement of siblings or restart to explain the missing reconciliation.

Grant the operator's identity the write access reconciliation needs: add update and patch on ocean.io whalewatchers (and whalewatchers/status if a status subresource is added to the CRD) plus any resources it must create or update, to ClusterRole whale-operator, and re-verify that .status.phase/observationCount change on the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96.

Make the reconciler's errors observable: run the container with unbuffered output (for example PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1) or explicit log flushing, then re-read the operator logs for Forbidden (403) or NotFound responses on whalewatchers writes; the container currently returns 0 log lines over the entire window, which hides whatever the loop is doing.

Compare the API group/version the operator code uses (inside the unreadable Secret mounted at /app) with the CRD's only served version v1, and inspect the WhaleWatcher objects' spec and status in app-96, before treating the RBAC gap as the sole cause.

gaps: The requested custom-crd runbook is not available for this target: fetch_skill returned status error with KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and stated the only runbook available is service-troubleshooting, which does not match a CRD reconciliation problem; no runbook steps could be executed, and the missing tool was an approved CRD-reconciliation runbook.

WhaleWatcher custom resources in app-96 could not be read: the Kubernetes tool's kind list has no whalewatchers resource (kubernetes_jq_query kind=whalewatchers returned INVALID_PARAMS), so the existence, spec and current status of the CRs, and whether status was ever written, are unknown; confirming them would need a client able to read ocean.io/v1 whalewatchers.

The operator container's logs returned 0 lines over the whole authorized window (both the default hour and the full 2026-11-20T07:25:22Z-2026-11-21T07:25:22Z range; view status no_data), so whether the operator attempted writes and was rejected (e.g. 403 Forbidden) is unobserved, not disproven.
The operator source is delivered by a Secret-backed volume mounted at /app; Secrets cannot be read by this Run, so operator.py's group/version, verb usage and namespace scope could not be verified.

Prometheus was unavailable for every call in this Run (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so apiserver_request_total by user/verb/code, kube-state-metrics and any reconciliation metrics are unknown rather than zero, and no error-rate baseline could be compared.
Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace evidence exists for this investigation.

The Kubernetes queries for Roles and RoleBindings in app-96 returned no_data (empty views 207965b1-3478-4352-9c3c-85e50f2a9ea5-t0 and -t1) and cannot be cited as proof of absence; a namespaced grant for the operator identity beyond the ClusterRole therefore remains unchecked, not disproven.

The app-96 stack was created about 40 seconds before the first observation (namespace 2026-11-21T07:24:43Z), so nothing about its state or the CRs' reconciliation earlier in the 24-hour window can be established from these reads.
The change_history integration is not available, so when the ClusterRole, CRD or operator deployment were authored or altered cannot be determined.
next_steps: Read the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 (spec and .status) with a client that can access ocean.io/v1 whalewatchers to confirm that reconciliation output is missing and to capture their generation versus status.

After the RBAC gap is addressed, capture the operator's log output for the API server response codes on whalewatchers writes (403 Forbidden versus 404 NotFound) to distinguish the read-only ClusterRole from a wrong status subresource path.
Restore Prometheus scraping so apiserver request metrics by user and response code, and kube-state-metrics for namespace app-96, can be queried for the incident window.
